definition_en: Draw Calibration Gap is the signed gap, in percentage points, between the average draw probability a forecaster assigned to a declared set of matches and the draw frequency that actually occurred in that same set, reported for the draw outcome alone.

fields.dcg_pp: mean_assigned - realized, percentage points, signed (positive = overestimates draws)
fields.devig_method: de-vig method, required (e.g. proportional / power), printed with the numbers
fields.market_dcg_pp: same gap for market-implied probabilities on the same set, always printed beside the model's
fields.matches_through: date of the last match in the set
fields.mean_assigned: average draw probability assigned over the set (market probabilities de-vigged first)
fields.paired_se_pp: paired SE: single gap sd(p_i - y_i)/sqrt(n); model-vs-market comparison sd of per-match (p_model - p_market) differences / sqrt(n)
fields.realized: actual draw frequency in the set
fields.se_pp: binomial SE of realized, sqrt(r(1-r)/n), percentage points
fields.set: league + window + n, declared before any gap is reported

fixtures.note: Combined DCG full precision -1.54pp; the check post printed -1.55pp from summing 2dp-rounded league means. Bucket table is exploratory: boundaries frozen after the aggregate was known, preregistered unchanged for 2024-25 / held-out leagues.
fixtures.source: football-data.co.uk 2023-24 CSVs (E0/I1/SP1), Bet365 closing 1X2, proportional de-vig
